word.name: enumerated-value-allowed
word.title: Enumerated Value Allowed
word.description: Each value of a field that a link makes enumerated is tapestry:<tapestryKey>, naming an element of the link's source concept that counts from the owner's point of view.

graphRule.name: enumerated-value-allowed
graphRule.says: each value of a field that a link makes enumerated is `tapestry:<tapestryKey>`, naming an element of the link's source concept that counts from the owner's point of view. A link is one `ENUMERATES` from the source concept's superset to the field's property node, carrying only its type (`graph enumerate`; ADR graph-operations-first-slice/0019). A field of type string holds one such value, and a list of strings any number, each judged on its own; a `null`, and a field left out, aren't judged. A value that names a node any other way, by its name, its slug or its address, isn't allowed. The allowed values are the source's elements as they are when a value is checked, read through the source's class thread from its superset, and no copy of them is kept: an element added to the source is allowed from then on, and one taken out of it, or deleted, no longer is, with no further call.
graphRule.kind: a graph rule, about the owner's and the admins' own element writes (D4). The link may have been made by `graph enumerate` or by today's `POST /api/normalize/enumerate`, which write the same edge. A value counts from the owner's point of view as a read's node does (ADR graph-operations-first-slice/0011): the instance's own, one with no author, or one whose author the owner's web of trust scores above the verified cutoff. So the same value can be allowed today and not tomorrow, as the owner's scores change.
graphRule.refusesOrReports: it refuses the write, before anything changes: `value-not-allowed` (400) when the JSON the write builds holds, at an enumerated field, a value that isn't a reference, a reference whose key names no node, or one naming a node that the source doesn't hold, or doesn't hold from the owner's point of view. The refusal names the field by its place under the concept's key, each value and why it isn't allowed, and the source concept by its name and its tapestryKey, and gives the way on: `graph resolve` turns a name into its key, `graph list-elements` on the source lists its elements, and `graph create-element` there adds one. Nothing that today's routes or an import write is judged (D15).
graphRule.check: for each concept of the items, the rule's first read finds its enumerated fields: each `ENUMERATES` from a superset to a property node that hangs, by a chain of `IS_A_PROPERTY_OF` through property nodes only, under the concept's primary property, each chain giving the field's place. An edge to a JSON schema node is never one, so firmware install's own enumerations, which end there with a `destinationPath`, aren't read, and a property hung on the schema node too, as today's enumerate route leaves one, is found by its chain. A concept with none costs that read alone. The second read judges every reference the items hold, all in one `UNWIND`. `graph enumerate` reports with the same check, over the property's concept's elements from their JSON, those whose values the link doesn't allow, and refuses none. Values already written aren't judged again: `rules check` (A10.31) will run it over every element, in a node form not built yet, and report each value that no longer names an allowed element.
graphRule.repair: none yet. `graph update-node` gives an element's field a reference, such as `--fields '{"project": "tapestry:<tapestryKey>"}'`, and `graph unenumerate` takes the link out, after which the field's values are judged by its schema alone.
graphRule.enforcedBy: the guards of `graph create-element`, `graph update-node` and `graph add-to-concept`, run in each write right after rule 7's, over the same JSON, once the write holds its locks: create-element's for the concept it names, update-node's for each concept whose section the call changes, naming every finding in one refusal, and add-to-concept's for the concept it names, when the call changes the node's JSON. The rule's code is in `src/operations/rules/enumerated-value-allowed.js`, and its two reads and its check are in `src/operations/catalog/graph/_enumerations.js`. It takes no lock of its own: a source changed by another write at the same moment can let through a value that no longer names an element, which `rules check` will find. Built in story graph-operations-first-slice #19 (ADR graph-operations-first-slice/0019).

code.summary: Each value of a field an ENUMERATES ends at is tapestry:<tapestryKey>, naming an element of the link's source concept that counts from the owner's point of view

refusals.when: The element's JSON holds, at a field a link makes enumerated, a value that isn't tapestry:<tapestryKey> of an element of the link's source concept from the owner's point of view: not a reference, a key that names no node, or a node the source doesn't hold, or doesn't hold from that point of view. The refusal names the field, each value and why, the source concept by name and key, and the way on: graph resolve, graph list-elements on the source, or graph create-element there
